job.title: Financial Accountant
job.description:
Who's hiring?
Centacare is one of South Australia's most trusted not-for-profits, supporting more than 20,000 South Australians each year. We're there for people doing it tough - whether they're navigating mental health challenges, domestic and family violence, homelessness, disability services, carer support or relationship breakdown. We show up with serious heart, vital services and relentless compassion.

Core to providing that support - consistently, sustainably and with impact - is our finance team. And right now, we're looking for a Financial Accountant who's ready to roll up their sleeves and make a difference.

So, what's the role?
This is a fantastic opportunity for a Financial Accountant who enjoys getting into the detail, takes pride in getting the numbers right and likes being part of a collaborative finance team.

Reporting to the Finance Manager, you'll be responsible for key financial accounting activities, including month-end processes, general ledger management, balance sheet reconciliations and payroll journals. You'll play an important role in ensuring the accuracy and integrity of financial information, maintaining strong financial controls and keeping reporting deadlines on track.

Working closely with the broader finance team, including Finance Business Partners, payroll and operational teams, you'll also have the opportunity to contribute to process improvements and systems enhancements across the organisation.

Here's what a typical week might look like:
  • Managing the general ledger and preparing monthly balance sheet reconciliations
  • Coordinating month-end processes, including accruals, journals and ensuring reporting deadlines are met
  • Preparing payroll journals and reconciliations, working closely with payroll and HR to resolve discrepancies
  • Managing fixed asset and depreciation schedules, along with grant income recognition
  • Assisting with year-end statutory accounts and liaising with internal and external auditors
  • Supporting the broader finance team and identifying opportunities to improve financial processes and systems
Enough about us—let's talk about whether this role is for you!
You're a detail-oriented Accountant who enjoys the technical side of accounting and takes pride in producing accurate, reliable financial information. You're organised, comfortable working to deadlines and have a knack for identifying discrepancies and working through problems.

Importantly, you're someone who thinks critically, asks questions and has the confidence to make decisions rather than simply following processes. You'll enjoy being hands-on, but you're also someone who sees the bigger picture and understands the importance of strong financial processes and controls.

Technically speaking, you:
  • Hold a degree in Accounting, Finance or Business (or equivalent experience)
  • Have solid experience in financial accounting, particularly month-end processes, general ledger management and balance sheet reconciliations
  • Have a sound understanding of accounting principles and standards, including accrual accounting, income recognition and lease accounting
  • Bring strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the confidence to investigate issues and make informed decisions
  • Have advanced Excel skills and enjoy working with complex financial data
  • Are highly organised, detail-oriented and comfortable working to deadlines
  • Communicate confidently with stakeholders, including internal and external auditors
  • Experience with TechnologyOne will be highly regarded
  • Hold (or are willing to obtain) a valid DHS Working with Children Check
What's in it for you?
  • A chance to do meaningful work in an organisation that helps thousands of South Australians
  • The opportunity to join a collaborative and supportive finance team
  • Career development, mentoring and ongoing learning opportunities
  • Hybrid working (WFH one day a week)
  • Access to NFP salary packaging benefits
Sound like your kind of role?
Click that apply button - we'd love to hear from you. Have further questions? Give Melanie at Mansfield & Co a call on 0411 471 822 for a confidential chat.

job.title: Business Performance & Commercial Analyst
job.description:
Who's hiring?
ForestrySA is a unique South Australian organisation with a lot more happening behind the scenes than you might expect!

Managing some of South Australia's most beautiful forests, ForestrySA's operations span commercial forestry, conservation, tourism, recreation and community education. From sustainable timber production to walking and mountain biking trails, campgrounds and school education programs, their work is incredibly diverse.

With an ambitious growth agenda and plenty of exciting opportunities on the horizon, it's a great time to join the business.

The office location is pretty special too! Based in the beautiful Kuitpo Forest, you'll be surrounded by stunning scenery and wildlife, with the opportunity to enjoy a forest walk on your lunch break.

So, what's the role?
Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, this newly created position will play an important role in supporting ForestrySA's growth plans and improving commercial decision-making across the business.

It's a hands-on, commercially focused role where you'll work closely with operational managers and the leadership team, providing the financial modelling, analysis and insights needed to assess opportunities, develop business cases and improve business performance.

You'll be involved in a broad range of projects and initiatives, with plenty of variety and the opportunity to make a genuine contribution.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Developing financial models, business cases and commercial evaluations to support new initiatives and investment decisions.
  • Analysing financial and operational performance, identifying trends, opportunities and areas for improvement.
  • Preparing cost-benefit analyses, forecasts and scenario modelling to support business planning.
  • Developing meaningful performance reports, dashboards and KPIs to support management decisions.
  • Working closely with managers across the business to understand operational challenges and identify commercial opportunities.
  • Supporting strategic projects, process improvements and initiatives designed to improve efficiency and business performance.
  • Preparing commercial insights and recommendations for the CFO, leadership team and Board.
What are we looking for?
We're looking for a commercially minded finance professional who enjoys getting into the detail, solving problems and working closely with people across a business.

Ideally, you'll be CA or CPA qualified, with experience in commercial analysis, financial modelling, business case development or a similar commercially focused finance role.

You'll bring:
  • Strong financial modelling and advanced Excel skills, with the ability to analyse complex information and develop practical recommendations.
  • Experience preparing business cases, commercial evaluations and performance reporting.
  • Well-developed analytical, critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to build relationships across all levels of a business.
  • A proactive, resourceful approach – you're comfortable asking questions, seeking out information and working through challenges.
  • The flexibility and adaptability to thrive in an evolving environment where priorities and opportunities may change.
Experience with Power BI would be advantageous, although it's not essential.
Just as importantly, you'll be personable, curious and collaborative. You'll enjoy getting out from behind your desk, understanding how different parts of the business operate and working with others to achieve great outcomes.

What's in it for you?
There's a lot to like about this opportunity. You'll be joining a supportive, collaborative team at a time when ForestrySA is looking to grow, innovate and explore new commercial opportunities.

As a newly created position, there's genuine scope to make the role your own, contribute ideas and have a direct impact on business decisions.
You'll also enjoy a unique working environment at Kuitpo Forest, with the flexibility to work from home one to two days per week.

How to apply
If you're looking for a commercially focused role with plenty of variety and the opportunity to contribute to an organisation that plays an important role in South Australia, we'd love to hear from you.

To apply, send your cover letter and resume by clicking APPLY below and we’ll handle the rest! For a confidential discussion, contact Melanie at Mansfield & Co on 0411 471 822.

job.title: Finance Manager
job.description:
Who’s hiring?

Spendless Shoes is a familiar name across Australia, helping customers find footwear for the whole family. With a national retail network and large-scale operations, there’s plenty happening behind the scenes to keep the business moving.

Reporting to the Group Chief Financial Officer, you’ll oversee and take accountability for day-to-day finance operations, support the financial performance of the business and help your team deliver accurate, timely work.

It’s an opportunity to bring your technical knowledge and people leadership together, with scope to improve processes and make a practical contribution to a well-known business.

So, what’s the role?

This is a hands-on Finance Manager position with accountability for the accuracy, integrity and timely delivery of Spendless Shoes’ financial accounts.

You’ll oversee accounting operations, manage cash flow and forecasting, and ensure reporting and statutory obligations are met. Working closely with the Group CFO, you’ll investigate discrepancies and provide clear visibility of the business’s financial position.

Leading the team is equally important. You’ll set clear expectations, provide guidance and mentoring, and ensure your team has the direction and support to deliver. You’ll be comfortable getting involved, resolving issues and taking responsibility for the quality of the function’s work.

A typical week might see you:
  • Overseeing day-to-day accounting operations, including revenue and cost allocations
  • Leading month-end close and ensuring the accuracy of the general ledger and balance sheet reconciliations
  • Maintaining cash forecasts and working closely with the Group CFO to monitor the daily cash position
  • Leading and supporting a team of four, managing priorities and reviewing work
  • Preparing and lodging BAS and other ATO compliance statements, and coordinating annual FBT information
  • Developing the annual budget and supporting effective cost control
  • Maintaining the asset register and reviewing financial information for accuracy and completeness
  • Overseeing financial systems, coordinating with external providers and supporting system upgrades
  • Identifying opportunities to improve processes, increase efficiency and reduce costs.
Who are you?

You’re a technically capable finance professional who enjoys taking
responsibility for an accounting function and helping a team perform at its best.

You’ve managed finance within a business with significant annual revenue and understand the accounting complexity, transaction volumes and reporting expectations that come with that scale. You can oversee the wider function while staying close enough to the detail to recognise when something needs further investigation.

Your approach to leadership matters just as much as your accounting knowledge. You’re approachable, communicate clearly and build productive working relationships. You know how to set expectations and hold people accountable while providing the guidance they need to succeed.

You’ll bring:
  • CA or CPA qualifications
  • Previous experience as a Finance Manager or in a comparable role within a large organisation with significant annual revenue
  • Thorough knowledge of financial accounting, month-end reporting, budgeting, cash flow management and cost control
  • Experience leading and developing a finance team
  • A hands-on approach to investigating accounting issues and providing practical technical guidance
  • Commercial awareness and confidence communicating financial information to senior stakeholders
  • Knowledge of relevant financial regulations and statutory obligations
  • Confidence using financial systems, with an interest in improving processes and reporting
  • Attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
What’s in it for you?
  • A permanent leadership role with Spendless Shoes, a well-known name in Australian retail
  • Ownership of the accounting function, reporting directly to the Group CFO
  • The opportunity to lead, mentor and develop a team of four
  • Scope to improve financial processes, systems and ways of working
  • A role that brings together technical accounting, commercial input and people leadership.
How to apply
If you’re a Finance Manager who enjoys taking ownership, developing a team and making a practical difference to a business, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply now, or for a confidential discussion, please contact Jacqueline Davey at Mansfield & Co Recruitment on 0493 552 504.

job.title: Senior Winemaker
job.description:
Who's hiring?
Fourth Wave Wine isn't your traditional wine business. Independent, family-owned and proudly Australian, they're behind some of the country's most recognisable and innovative wine brands, including Little Giant, Tread Softly, Elephant in the Room and Farm Hand.

With a strong presence across Australia and international markets, Fourth Wave has built a successful and growing business by doing things differently. They're continually exploring new products and emerging categories, from organic and preservative-free wines through to lower-alcohol, zero-alcohol and flavoured drinks.

It's a progressive, fun and commercially minded business with an ambitious, high-performing team. The culture is driven, capable and energised, with people who enjoy what they do, embrace new ideas and are genuinely excited about where the business is heading.

With continued growth comes the opportunity to welcome a Senior Winemaker into this newly created position.

So, what's the role?
This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced Winemaker who's keen to broaden their experience beyond traditional winery operations and get involved in the bigger picture of the wine business.

Working closely with the Chief Winemaker, you'll play a key role in managing wine production across a diverse portfolio of brands, with a particular focus on sourcing, blending, finishing, bottling and quality assurance.

Rather than overseeing the winemaking process from grape to bottle, you'll work with an extensive network of Australian and international wine suppliers and production partners to ensure the finished products deliver on quality, consistency and style.

It's a hands-on role with plenty of variety. One day you might be assessing wines from international suppliers, the next overseeing a bottling run, reviewing wine quality or contributing to the development of an exciting new product.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Sourcing, assessing and selecting wines from local and international suppliers.
  • Preparing and refining blends to meet brand styles and specifications.
  • Overseeing bottling operations, including preparation, quality checks and final product sign-off.
  • Working closely with external wineries, bottling facilities and production partners.
  • Contributing to new product development, including emerging wine and drinks categories.
  • Developing an understanding of the commercial considerations behind production, packaging and supply decisions.
Based from home in Adelaide, you'll regularly visit bottling and production facilities across metropolitan Adelaide and South Australia's wine regions, including the Barossa, McLaren Vale, Adelaide Hills and Coonawarra. There will also be occasional interstate and (potentially) international travel.

You'll have plenty of opportunity to take ownership, contribute ideas and develop your skills, with the support and mentoring of an experienced Chief Winemaker.

What are we looking for?
We're looking for a qualified Winemaker who brings strong technical knowledge, a practical approach and an interest in the broader commercial side of the wine industry.

You'll be comfortable working across wine preparation, finishing and bottling, with the ability to assess quality, solve problems and make sound decisions.
Just as importantly, we're looking for someone who will thrive in Fourth Wave's culture. You'll be motivated, energetic and commercially curious, with a genuine growth mindset and a willingness to challenge how things have traditionally been done.

You'll enjoy being part of a high-performing team, take pride in your work and have the initiative and confidence to manage your responsibilities independently, while staying connected and collaborating closely with colleagues and production partners.

Experience with preservative-free, lower-alcohol or flavoured drinks would be an advantage, as would exposure to multiple production partners, but neither is essential.

Why consider this opportunity?
You'll join a successful, family-owned business that's growing, innovating and making its mark in the Australian and international wine markets.

There's a lot to like about this opportunity:
  • A newly created position offering variety, autonomy and room to grow.
  • The chance to work across an exciting range of brands and innovative new products.
  • A progressive, fun and high-performing team that genuinely enjoys working together.
  • Direct mentoring from the Chief Winemaker and exposure to the broader commercial wine business.
  • The flexibility of working from home in Adelaide, balanced with regular visits to wineries and production facilities.
  • A competitive base salary, plus a car allowance and an annual wine allowance!
Interested?
If you're an experienced Winemaker who's ready for something a little different and would enjoy being part of an ambitious, growing business, we'd love to hear from you.

For a confidential discussion, please contact Melanie Mansfield at Mansfield & Co Recruitment on 0411 471 822.

job.title: Administration & Finance Officer
job.description:
Who's hiring?
Distribution 360 are a proudly South Australian business who are doing their bit to create a cleaner environment.

We work with local councils, businesses and residents to safely remove and reliably recycle rubbish across our state. We're focussed on getting the job done quickly and cleanly and offer a range of services including our end-to-end bulky goods removal and mattress recycling.

Ultimately, we're a passionate group of locals who are doing their bit to create a rubbish-responsible future for our planet.

We're on the hunt for an Administration & Finance Officer to work in a job share arrangement, keeping our office – and our drivers – organised and on track.

So, what's the role?
You'll be the organised person helping keep everything on track behind the scenes. From coordinating daily jobs to managing accounts and customer communication, you'll take ownership of the administration that keeps the business running smoothly.

It's a varied role where you can work autonomously, manage your priorities and make a tangible contribution to the day-to-day operation.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Keeping jobs on track: Reviewing the previous day's dockets, reconciling job details and invoicing completed work.
  • Managing accounts: Looking after accounts receivable and payable, processing payments and completing reconciliations.
  • Coordinating the daily schedule: Helping plan upcoming jobs and coordinating logistics with drivers and customers.
  • Keeping communication flowing: Managing emails, calls and customer enquiries to ensure everyone has the information they need.
  • Reporting and office support: Preparing regular reports and keeping your workspace organised and running smoothly.
What are we looking for?
You're naturally organised, reliable and someone who gets satisfaction from bringing order to a busy day. You can manage your own workload, keep an eye on the details and make sure things don't fall through the cracks.

You'll ideally bring:
  • Experience in administration, accounts support or a similar office-based role.
  • Confidence with invoicing, accounts receivable and payable, and reconciliations.
  • Strong computer skills, particularly with Outlook and Excel.
  • A friendly, practical approach to customer service and problem-solving.
  • The ability to work independently, take ownership and manage competing priorities.
Experience with Cash Flow Manager would be an advantage, but it's not essential.

Most importantly, you're someone who takes pride in doing a good job, communicates well and can be relied upon to keep things moving.

What's in it for you?
Flexibility that works both ways.  This role offers 3 days per week, with a predictable routine and some flexibility to accommodate your schedule.
  • Part-time hours: 3 days per week, with the opportunity to pick up additional shifts by agreement.
  • A manageable daily routine: Typically starting around 9am, with on-site work wrapping up around 3pm.
  • Work-from-home flexibility: A short remote period monitoring calls and emails until 5pm helps keep things covered.
  • A say in your schedule: Regular office days can be negotiated, with one work-from-home day each week.
You'll be joining a local business where your contribution matters. You'll have the autonomy to manage your responsibilities and the satisfaction of knowing your work helps keep the operation running smoothly.

Most importantly, we are passionate about offering a workplace where our team feels valued.

How do I apply?
If you fit the brief and are excited by the opportunity to contribute to a great local business who is doing their bit for the world, we can't wait to hear from you.

For a confidential discussion, contact Tracy Frankenfeld at Mansfield & Co on 0493 703 697 or tracy@mansfieldandco.com.au

job.title: Accounts Payable Officer
job.description:
Enjoy working your way through a to-do list and knowing everything adds up? We’re looking for an Accounts Payable Officer who takes pride in getting the details right and keeping things moving.

So, what’s the role?

Joining an established business on a six-month contract, you’ll report to the Management Accountant and look after day-to-day accounts payable, alongside other finance and administration tasks.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Processing supplier invoices, checking approvals and supporting documentation
  • Reconciling supplier accounts, arranging payments and resolving queries
  • Processing daily bank transactions and assisting with international purchases
  • Processing expense claims and reconciling AMEX transactions
  • Completing month-end reconciliations
  • Helping with accounts receivable enquiries and fleet administration
What are we looking for?

You’ll bring previous accounts payable experience, a careful eye for detail and an organised approach to your day. You’re comfortable managing your own workload, following up outstanding items and seeing tasks through to completion.

You’ll also have:
  • Confidence using Excel, Word and accounting systems
  • Clear, professional communication skills
  • The ability to juggle priorities and meet payment deadlines
  • A willingness to help with the broader team’s accounts and administration needs
  • Availability to commit to six months, working five days a week.
What’s in it for you?
  • Amazing offices you’ll enjoy coming into each day
  • A six-month opportunity to settle in and make the role your own
  • Variety across accounts payable, finance and administration
  • The satisfaction of taking ownership and keeping accounts accurate and up to date.
If you enjoy getting stuck into your work and seeing a job through, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now.

job.title: Customer Support Officer
job.description:
Our client is a growing business based in Lonsdale, looking for a Customer Service Officer to help with customer enquiries and day-to-day order support. This temporary role offers five days per week, with an ASAP start.

This role will suit someone who enjoys helping customers, has a good phone manner and can confidently handle enquiries while learning about a new product range. You don’t need to have all the answers from day one, but you will need to be comfortable taking messages, asking questions and passing more detailed enquiries to the appropriate person.

So, what's the role?

You’ll support the team with day-to-day customer service and administration, including:
  • Answering incoming calls, taking clear messages and escalating enquiries where required
  • Responding to basic customer emails about products, orders and deliveries
  • Assisting with order processing and maintaining accurate customer records
  • Liaising with internal teams on customer requests and order updates
  • Providing general administrative support.
What are we looking for?

We’re looking for someone with:
  • Previous customer service experience, ideally within a product-based business
  • A friendly, confident phone manner and clear written communication
  • The confidence to handle calls while building your product knowledge
  • Good attention to detail and the ability to keep track of customer enquiries
  • Confidence using computer systems and learning new processes
  • Availability to start ASAP and work five days per week in Lonsdale.
What’s in it for you?
  • An immediate opportunity to put your customer service experience to use
  • A supportive team, with training on products and systems
  • Variety across customer enquiries, order support and administration.
If you’re available to start ASAP and enjoy being the person customers can turn to for help, we’d love to hear from you.

job.title: Financial Accountant
job.description:
Who's hiring?

For over 25 years, Caledonia Group has delivered scaffolding, rope access, insulation, cladding and engineering solutions across the mining, energy, infrastructure and commercial sectors in Australia, New Zealand and beyond. We support some of the biggest and most complex projects in the region, backed by uncompromising safety standards and a leadership team with deep industry experience. Just as importantly, we're a genuinely good place to work — a close, down-to-earth crew that's small enough that everyone knows everyone, where people pick up the phone rather than fire off an email, and where Friday afternoons, team lunches and the odd toolbox pizza are all part of how the place ticks. As we continue to grow, we're looking for a Financial Accountant to keep our reporting sharp and our numbers telling a clear story.

So, what's the role?

Reporting to an experienced Finance Director, you'll take ownership of month-end management and reporting across the Group. You'll work closely alongside the broader finance team, and partner with Directors and operational teams — including Claims and Contracts Administrators across SA, WA, NSW and New Zealand — to make sure the numbers land with the people who rely on them.

There's a real appetite here for someone who'll improve things rather than simply maintain them — the general ledger could do with a tidy, and there's scope to sharpen reporting, controls and systems as you go. It's an ideal role for someone with sound technical grounding who's ready to take on more than their current position allows.

Here's what a typical week might look like:
  • Owning the month-end close and preparing consolidated P&L, balance sheet and cashflow reporting
  • Producing monthly management packs with variance analysis and commentary — and the operational insight that helps teams act on them
  • Completing intercompany and balance sheet reconciliations across all entities
  • Supporting the annual budget, quarterly reforecasts and job/project profitability analysis
  • Delivering KPIs and decision-support to the Finance Director and operational leaders
  • Preparing weekly and monthly cashflow forecasts, monitoring working capital and supporting banking and financing arrangements
  • Owning compliance across the Group, including BAS, and strengthening financial controls, governance and the annual audit
  • Approving payroll and supporting the wider finance team
  • Driving process and system improvements across finance and reporting
Enough about us—let's talk about whether this role is for you!

You're someone who enjoys getting into the detail, takes pride in accurate work and likes building relationships across a business rather than staying behind the numbers. You're proactive, organised and happiest when you're improving a process, not just keeping it running.

Technically speaking, you:
  • Hold a degree in Accounting, Finance or a related discipline, with CA or CPA completed or underway
  • Have sound financial accounting fundamentals — month-end close, journals, accruals and reconciliations
  • Bring strong compliance skills — including BAS — along with balance sheet reconciliation experience
  • Have exposure to multi-entity reporting and consolidation, or the appetite to pick it up quickly
  • Are a confident communicator who can work with Directors and operational teams and explain the numbers to people outside finance
  • Bring the kind of operational insight that turns reporting into something teams can act on
  • Have working knowledge of payroll (an advantage)
  • Have experience with MYOB and Xero, or similar systems including Modano (an advantage)
A commercial background in a project-based or operationally driven business will be well regarded, though it isn't essential.

What's in it for you?
  • Join a $100m+ national construction business in a stable, growing sector
  • Work alongside an experienced Finance Director and respected leadership team
  • A down-to-earth team where everyone knows everyone, with flexible core hours and one day a week from home
  • A long-term, secure career path with genuine room to grow
  • Competitive salary 
How to apply?

Click that apply button — we'd love to hear from you. For a confidential discussion, contact Tracy Frankenfeld at Mansfield & Co on 0493 703 697 or tracy@mansfieldandco.com.au
